description: Erbium is a chemical element with symbol Er and atomic number 68. It is a silvery-white solid metal when artificially isolated and a lanthanide, rare-earth element originally found in the gadolinite mine in Ytterby, Sweden. Natural erbium is always found in chemical combination with other elements.
uses: Erbium's principal uses involve its pink-colored Er3+ ions for optical fluorescent properties in laser applications, particularly in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers for optical communications at 1550 nm wavelength. Medical applications in dermatology and dentistry rely on erbium ion's 2940 nm emission for laser surgery and dental procedures. Erbium compounds are also used as phosphor activators, in infrared-absorbing glass, and in crystal growth applications.
characteristics: Pure erbium metal is malleable, soft, and stable in air without rapid oxidation. Its salts are rose-colored, and the element exhibits characteristic sharp absorption spectra bands in visible light, ultraviolet, and near infrared. Erbium is ferromagnetic below 19 K, antiferromagnetic between 19 and 80 K, and paramagnetic above 80 K, and it burns readily in oxygen to form erbium(III) oxide while reacting slowly with cold water and quickly with hot water.
